results.title: Orientation-preserving reparametrization of the circle
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: An orientation-preserving smooth reparametrization of the circle is given by maps $f, g \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, both $C^\infty$ and inverse to each other ($g(f(t)) = t$ and $f(g(t)) = t$ for all $t$), such that $f(t + 2\pi) = f(t) + 2\pi$ and $g(t + 2\pi) = g(t) + 2\pi$ for all $t$, and $f$ is strictly increasing. Here $f$ is a lift of the reparametrization and $g$ is a lift of its inverse.

results.title: Identity reparametrization of the circle
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The identity circle reparametrization has lift and inverse lift both equal to the identity map of $\mathbb{R}$.

results.title: Inverse circle reparametrization
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The inverse of a circle reparametrization with lift $f$ and inverse lift $f^{-1}$ is the circle reparametrization whose lift is $f^{-1}$ and whose inverse lift is $f$.

results.title: Composition of circle reparametrizations
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: If $\sigma$ and $\tau$ are circle reparametrizations with lifts $f_\sigma, f_\tau$ and inverse lifts $g_\sigma, g_\tau$, their composition (first $\sigma$, then $\tau$) is the circle reparametrization with lift $f_\tau \circ f_\sigma$ and inverse lift $g_\sigma \circ g_\tau$.

results.title: Isotopy of parametrized knots
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Two parametrized knots $\gamma_1, \gamma_2$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ are isotopic (oriented ambient isotopy) if there are a smooth ambient isotopy of $\mathbb{R}^3$ with forward family $H_t$ and an orientation-preserving reparametrization of the circle with lift $f$ such that $H_1(\gamma_1(t)) = \gamma_2(f(t))$ for every $t \in \mathbb{R}$.

results.title: Isotopy of parametrized links
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Two parametrized links in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with $n$ components $\gamma^1_i$ and $\gamma^2_i$ ($i < n$) are isotopic (oriented, labeled ambient isotopy) if there are a single smooth ambient isotopy of $\mathbb{R}^3$ with forward family $H_t$ and, for each $i < n$, an orientation-preserving reparametrization of the circle with lift $f_i$, such that $H_1(\gamma^1_i(t)) = \gamma^2_i(f_i(t))$ for every $i < n$ and every…

results.title: Trace of a parametrized link
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The trace of a parametrized link $L$ in Euclidean 3-space is the union of the images of its component curves: the set of all points $\gamma(t)$, where $\gamma$ is a component of $L$ and $t \in \mathbb{R}$.

results.title: Total contour length of a parametrized link
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link in Euclidean 3-space with components $\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_n$, each a $2\pi$-periodic curve. The total contour length of $L$ is the sum over all components $\gamma_i$ of the contour length of $\gamma_i$ on one period $[0, 2\pi]$. It is a value in $[0, \infty]$.

results.title: Ropelength ratio of a parametrized link
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a parametrized link $L$, the ropelength ratio of $L$ is its total contour length divided by the thickness of its trace (the union of the images of its components), a value in $[0, \infty]$ computed with the division of $[0, \infty]$.

results.title: Ropelength of a parametrized link
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a parametrized link $L$ with $n$ components, the ropelength of $L$ is the infimum, in $[0, \infty]$, of the ropelength ratios of all parametrized links $L'$ with $n$ components that are isotopic to $L$. It is the ropelength of the oriented, labeled ambient-isotopy type of $L$.

results.title: Ropelength is at most the ratio of any isotopic link
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ and $L'$ be parametrized links with $n$ components. If $L'$ is isotopic to $L$, then the ropelength of $L$ is at most the ropelength ratio of $L'$.

results.title: Ropelength is at most the ropelength ratio
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every parametrized link $L$ with $n$ components, the ropelength of $L$ is at most the ropelength ratio of $L$.

results.title: Ropelength is an isotopy invariant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ be parametrized links with $n$ components. If $L_1$ is isotopic to $L_2$ (by an oriented, labeled ambient isotopy), then the ropelength of $L_1$ equals the ropelength of $L_2$.

results.title: Parametrized knot as a one-component link
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A parametrized knot $K$ determines the parametrized link with one component, whose single component is $K$; the pairwise disjointness condition holds trivially.

results.title: Isotopic knots give isotopic one-component links
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $K_1$ and $K_2$ are parametrized knots and $K_1$ is isotopic to $K_2$, then the one-component parametrized link of $K_1$ is isotopic to the one-component parametrized link of $K_2$.

results.title: Ropelength of a parametrized knot
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The ropelength of a parametrized knot $K$ is the ropelength of the one-component parametrized link determined by $K$: the infimum, in $[0, \infty]$, of the ropelength ratios of all one-component parametrized links that are isotopic to the one-component link of $K$.

results.title: Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^3$
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The ambient space of the knots here is $\mathbb{R}^3$ with its standard Euclidean inner product.

results.title: Oriented smooth knot
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: An oriented smooth knot in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is a smooth map $\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ that is $2\pi$-periodic, injective on $[0, 2\pi)$, and an immersion, meaning $\gamma'(t) \ne 0$ for every real $t$. The orientation is the one induced by the parametrization.

results.title: Two-component link
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: An oriented two-component smooth link in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is a pair $(K, L)$ of oriented smooth knots whose images in $\mathbb{R}^3$ are disjoint.

results.title: Smooth ambient isotopy of $\mathbb{R}^3$
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A smooth ambient isotopy of $\mathbb{R}^3$ consists of two families of maps $H_t, G_t \colon \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ indexed by $t \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $(t, x) \mapsto H_t(x)$ and $(t, x) \mapsto G_t(x)$ are smooth ($C^\infty$) maps $\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$, $G_t$ is a two-sided inverse of $H_t$ for every $t$, and $H_0$ is the identity. In particular every $H_t$ is a…

results.title: Ambient isotopy of oriented knots
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $K_1$ and $K_2$ be oriented knots, each given by its $2\pi$-periodic parametrization. They are ambient-isotopic if there are a smooth ambient isotopy $(\Phi_t)_{t \in \mathbb{R}}$ of $\mathbb{R}^3$ and an orientation-preserving smooth reparametrization $\sigma$ of the circle such that $\Phi_1(K_1(t)) = K_2(\sigma(t))$ for every real $t$. Here an orientation-preserving smooth reparametrization of the circle is a…

results.title: Ambient isotopy of oriented two-component links
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $L = (K, J)$ and $L' = (K', J')$ be oriented two-component links, each knot given by its $2\pi$-periodic parametrization. Then $L$ and $L'$ are ambient-isotopic if there are a smooth ambient isotopy $(\Phi_t)_{t \in \mathbb{R}}$ of $\mathbb{R}^3$ and orientation-preserving smooth reparametrizations $\sigma$, $\tau$ of the circle such that $\Phi_1(K(t)) = K'(\sigma(t))$ and $\Phi_1(J(t)) = J'(\tau(t))$ for every…

results.title: Reflection in the $xy$-plane
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The reflection of $\mathbb{R}^3$ through the $xy$-plane is the map $(x, y, z) \mapsto (x, y, -z)$.

results.title: Chiral knot
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $K \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ be an oriented smooth knot, and let $\rho(x, y, z) = (x, y, -z)$ be the reflection of $\mathbb{R}^3$ through the $xy$-plane. Call $\sigma \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ an orientation-preserving reparametrization of the circle if it is a strictly increasing smooth bijection with smooth inverse satisfying $\sigma(t + 2\pi) = \sigma(t) + 2\pi$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$,…

results.title: Topological ambient isotopy
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A topological ambient isotopy of $\mathbb{R}^3$ is a family of maps $H_t : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$, indexed by $t \in \mathbb{R}$, together with a family $G_t : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ such that $(t, x) \mapsto H_t(x)$ and $(t, x) \mapsto G_t(x)$ are continuous, $G_t$ is a two-sided inverse of $H_t$ for every $t$ (so each $H_t$ is a homeomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^3$), and $H_0$ is the identity.

results.title: Topological ambient isotopy of subsets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Two subsets $A$ and $B$ of $\mathbb{R}^3$ are unoriented topologically ambient isotopic if there is a topological ambient isotopy $(H_t)$ of $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose time-one map carries $A$ onto $B$, that is, $H_1(A) = B$.

results.title: Closed unit disk in the plane
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The closed unit Euclidean disk $\{(x, y) \in \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R} \mid x^2 + y^2 \le 1\}$, the source of the parametrization of a slicing disk.

results.title: Unit circle in the plane
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The unit Euclidean circle $\{(x, y) \in \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R} \mid x^2 + y^2 = 1\}$, the source of the boundary of a slicing disk.

results.title: Closed upper half-space
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The closed upper half-space in $\mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}$ is the set $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, \infty)$ of points $(x, s)$ with $s \ge 0$.

results.title: Model interior $2$-plane
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The model interior $2$-plane in $\mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}$ is the set of points $((x_1, x_2, x_3), t)$ with $x_2 = x_3 = 0$, where $x_1$ and $t$ are arbitrary. It is the local model for interior local flatness of an embedded $2$-disk.

results.title: Model half-plane
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The model half-plane is the set of pairs $((p_1, p_2, p_3), s)$ in $\mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}$ with $p_2 = p_3 = 0$ and $s \ge 0$. It is a copy of the closed half-plane $\mathbb{R} \times [0, \infty)$, with coordinates $p_1$ and $s$, lying in the upper half-space $s \ge 0$.

results.title: Smoothly slice (smooth knot version)
results.caption: Definition

A smooth knot $K$ is smoothly slice if there is a smooth ($C^\infty$) map $f : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}$ such that $f$ is injective on $\Delta$; for every $p \in \Delta$ the last coordinate of $f(p)$ is nonnegative, and it is $0$…

results.caption: Definition

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $q \in \mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}$ and $D : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}$. results.title: Topologically slice (smooth knot version)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Write points of $\mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}$ as $(x, s)$ with $x = (x_1, x_2, x_3)$. Let $H = \{(x, s) : s \ge 0\}$ be the closed upper half-space, $P = \{(x, s) : x_2 = x_3 = 0\}$ the model plane and $P_+ = P \cap H$ the model half-plane, and let $D^2 = \{(a, b) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : a^2 + b^2 \le 1\}$ and $S^1 = \{(a, b) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : a^2 + b^2 = 1\}$. A smooth knot $K$ is topologically slice if there is a…

results.title: Parametrization of a closed polyline
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $v_0, \dots, v_{n-1}$ be a list of $n \ge 1$ points of $\mathbb{R}^3$. The polyline curve is the $n$-periodic map $\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ with $\gamma(k + \alpha) = (1 - \alpha) v_k + \alpha v_{k+1}$ for integers $0 \le k < n$ and reals $0 \le \alpha < 1$, where indices are taken modulo $n$ (so $v_n = v_0$). For the empty list the curve is constantly $0$.

results.title: PL knot (closed polyline)
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A PL knot is a list $v_0, \dots, v_{n-1}$ of points of $\mathbb{R}^3$ with $n \ge 3$, viewed as the vertices, in order, of the closed polyline with edges from $v_i$ to $v_{i+1}$ for $i < n - 1$ and from $v_{n-1}$ back to $v_0$.

results.title: Image of a PL knot
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $K$ be a PL knot with vertices $v_0, \dots, v_{n-1}$. Its image is the subset of $\mathbb{R}^3$ traced by the closed polyline through these vertices: the image of the half-open interval $[0, n)$ under the parametrization that sends $k + \alpha$, for an integer $0 \le k < n$ and a real $0 \le \alpha < 1$, to $(1 - \alpha) v_k + \alpha v_{k+1}$, with indices taken modulo $n$.

results.title: Simple PL knot
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A PL knot $K$ with vertices $v_0, \dots, v_{n-1}$ is simple if its closed polyline parametrization, which sends $k + \alpha$, for an integer $0 \le k < n$ and a real $0 \le \alpha < 1$, to $(1 - \alpha) v_k + \alpha v_{k+1}$ (indices modulo $n$), is injective on the half-open interval $[0, n)$.

results.title: Smooth representative of a PL knot
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A smooth knot $J$ is a smooth representative of the piecewise-linear knot $K$ if the image of $J$ and the image of $K$ are unoriented topologically ambient isotopic in $\mathbb{R}^3$: some topological ambient isotopy $(H_t)$ of $\mathbb{R}^3$ satisfies $H_1(\operatorname{im} J) = \operatorname{im} K$.

results.title: Smoothly slice (PL knot version)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A PL knot $K$ is smoothly slice if there is a smooth knot $J$ that is smoothly slice and is a smooth representative of $K$: for some topological ambient isotopy $(H_t)$ of $\mathbb{R}^3$, the map $H_1$ carries the image of $J$ onto the image (trace) of the polyline $K$.

results.title: Topologically slice (PL knot version)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A PL knot $K$ is topologically slice if there is a smooth knot $J$ that is a smooth representative of $K$, meaning that the image of $J$ and the image of $K$ are unoriented topologically ambient isotopic subsets of $\mathbb{R}^3$, and such that $J$ is topologically slice as a smooth knot.

results.title: Point from three coordinates
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For real numbers $x$, $y$, $z$, this is the point $(x, y, z)$ of the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^3$.

results.title: Braid closure traversal state
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A traversal state for tracing the closure of a braid consists of the current strand position, a natural number, and the list of points of $\mathbb{R}^3$ accumulated so far, in order, as vertices of the polyline.

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let a traversal state consist of a current strand position $p \in \mathbb{N}$ and a list of vertices in $\mathbb{R}^3$, let $w \in \mathbb{Z}$ be a braid generator with $i = |w|$, and let $z_{\mathrm{top}}, z_{\mathrm{bot}} \in \mathbb{R}$. results.title: Tracing a strand through a braid word
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a traversal state $s$, a braid word $w_0 w_1 \cdots w_{m-1}$ (a list of integers) and a starting index $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the one-crossing step is applied to the state for each generator in turn, starting from $s$: the generator $w_j$ is applied with top height $-(k + j)$ and bottom height $-(k + j + 1)$. The result is the final state; for the empty word it is $s$.

results.title: One pass of the braid closure
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $w$ be a braid word (a list of integers) of length $m$. Starting from a traversal state, one pass applies the letters of $w$ in order as crossings, the $k$-th letter (counting from $0$) occupying the slab $-(k+1) \le z \le -k$; this moves the state to a strand position $p$ and appends the crossing vertices. results.title: Iterated braid-closure passes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a braid word $w$, a number $f$ of remaining passes and a traversal state $S$, the iteration returns $S$ when $f = 0$. When $f > 0$ it applies one pass of $w$ to $S$, obtaining a state $S'$; it returns $S'$ if the strand position of $S'$ is $1$, and otherwise iterates on $S'$ with $f - 1$ passes remaining.

results.title: Polyline closure of a braid word
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $w = w_0 w_1 \cdots w_{m-1}$ be a braid word (a list of integers, where $i > 0$ stands for $\sigma_i$ and $-i$ for $\sigma_i^{-1}$). If $m = 0$, the value is the junk list $(0, 0, 0)$, $(1, 0, 0)$, $(0, 1, 0)$. Otherwise the value is a list of vertices in $\mathbb{R}^3$ tracing the closure of $w$ as one polyline component. results.title: Braid word for the Conway knot
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The braid word $\sigma_1^{-2} \sigma_2 \sigma_1^{-1} \sigma_2 \sigma_1^{-1} \sigma_3 \sigma_2^{-2} \sigma_3^{2}$ on $4$ strands, encoded as the list of integers $[-1, -1, 2, -1, 2, -1, 3, -2, -2, 3, 3]$, where an entry $i > 0$ stands for the generator $\sigma_i$ and $-i$ for $\sigma_i^{-1}$. It has length $11$ and writhe $-1$, and is a braid word for the Conway knot 11n34.

results.title: The Conway knot
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Conway knot 11n34 as a piecewise-linear closed polyline in $\mathbb{R}^3$: its vertices are those of the polyline closure, on $4$ strands, of the braid word $\sigma_1^{-2} \sigma_2 \sigma_1^{-1} \sigma_2 \sigma_1^{-1} \sigma_3 \sigma_2^{-2} \sigma_3^{2}$ for the Conway knot.

results.title: Knots as parametrized knots
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A knot in $\mathbb{R}^3$, given by a smooth $2\pi$-periodic immersion $\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ that is injective on $[0, 2\pi)$, is sent to the parametrized knot with the same parametrization $\gamma$.

results.title: Parametrized knots as knots
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A parametrized knot in $\mathbb{R}^3$, given by a smooth $2\pi$-periodic immersion $\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ that is injective on $[0, 2\pi)$, is sent to the knot with the same parametrization $\gamma$.

results.title: Knots are the same as parametrized knots
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Sending a knot in $\mathbb{R}^3$ to the parametrized knot with the same parametrization is a bijection from knots to parametrized knots, whose inverse sends a parametrized knot to the knot with the same parametrization.

results.title: Conway-knot circle reparametrizations as Euclidean ones
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An orientation-preserving smooth reparametrization of the circle in the sense of the Conway knot statements, given by a smooth strictly increasing map $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ with smooth two-sided inverse $g$ such that $f(t + 2\pi) = f(t) + 2\pi$ and $g(t + 2\pi) = g(t) + 2\pi$ for all $t$, is sent to the circle reparametrization, in the sense of parametrized links, with the same lift $f$ and inverse lift…

results.title: Euclidean circle reparametrizations as Conway-knot ones
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A circle reparametrization in the sense of parametrized links, given by a smooth strictly increasing map $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ with smooth two-sided inverse $g$ such that $f(t + 2\pi) = f(t) + 2\pi$ and $g(t + 2\pi) = g(t) + 2\pi$ for all $t$, is sent to the orientation-preserving smooth reparametrization of the circle in the sense of the Conway knot statements with the same lift $f$ and inverse lift $g$.

results.title: Isotopy of knots agrees with isotopy of parametrized knots
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all knots $K_1$ and $K_2$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$, $K_1$ and $K_2$ are ambient isotopic if and only if the parametrized knots with the same parametrizations as $K_1$ and $K_2$ are ambient isotopic as parametrized knots.

results.title: Two-component links as labeled links
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A two-component link in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with first component $K$ and second component $L$ is sent to the labeled parametrized link with two components whose component $0$ is the parametrized knot with the same parametrization as $K$ and whose component $1$ is the parametrized knot with the same parametrization as $L$.

results.title: Labeled two-component links as two-component links
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A labeled parametrized link with two components $0$ and $1$ is sent to the two-component link in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose first component is the knot with the same parametrization as component $0$ and whose second component is the knot with the same parametrization as component $1$.

results.title: Two-component link isotopy agrees with labeled link isotopy
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ be oriented two-component smooth links in $\mathbb{R}^3$, and regard each as an oriented labeled smooth link with two components, whose component $0$ is its first component and whose component $1$ is its second. Then $L_1$ and $L_2$ are ambient isotopic, meaning that a single smooth ambient isotopy carries each component of $L_1$ onto the corresponding component of $L_2$ up to…

results.title: Non-isotopic two-component links exist
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist two oriented smooth two-component links $L_1$ and $L_2$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ that are not ambient isotopic as oriented links with ordered components: no ambient isotopy of $\mathbb{R}^3$ carries the first component of $L_1$ to the first component of $L_2$ and the second component of $L_1$ to the second component of $L_2$, each up to an orientation-preserving reparametrization of the circle.

results.title: Existence of non-isotopic knots
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There are two oriented smooth knots $K_1$ and $K_2$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ that are not ambient-isotopic.
